authority: external market research only; no Meme Machine trade outcomes used for calibration
purpose: Calibrate high-multiple runner survival, Current-to-Survivor exposure continuity, and bounded staged scaling.

evidence.window: 60 days; 36h post-alert price window; only takeovers that rose at least 10%
evidence.limitation: Small, CTO-specific selected sample; useful for timing shape, not a population-wide Pump return estimate.

evidence.window: 45 days; minute snapshots for 36h after alert
evidence.limitation: Small sample; the source explicitly states the record does not statistically separate delayed/confirmed entry from alert entry.

evidence.window: 2026-08-25 through 2026-10-01; later price reading at least six hours after migration
evidence.implication: Do not convert the bridge into blind post-migration holding or lower Survivor age for every migration. Continuity is reserved for already-proven Current winners with fresh structural safety.
Pons right-tail moves can be materially developed by the existing six-hour Survivor threshold and can continue into 20h+ ages.

evidence.limitation: Rolling-window returns do not reconstruct exact peak-to-trough sequencing. They do directly demonstrate extreme intermediate volatility while the asset was still a large 24h winner.
Robinhood-chain context, not used as proof that every extreme move belongs to the Pons strategy universe.

calibration_conclusions: Fixed-clock exits are incompatible with the observed Pump right tail because a material share of measured winners peak many hours after Current horizons.
Blind early post-migration extension is rejected: the broad migration population has very high failure incidence.
A same-lifecycle bridge should be conditional on an already-proven Current winner and fresh structural safety, avoiding sell/rebuy and duplicate exposure.
High-multiple price trails must scale with accrued gain; fixed return-point giveback becomes mechanically too tight at large multiples.
Scaling is an optional amplifier after winner proof. Base-runner retention must not depend on a scale event.
